askus.li

23 Sep 23 Sep
11:39 p.m.
Hi All,

Two implementation defects in the Aigis-Sig$^+$ reference code are reported below. Runtime witnesses are for parameter set I (Aigis-sig1). The extra `polyz_unpack` is present in the published `polyvec.c` for parameter sets I, II and III.

Detected and reproduced autonomously by Askus Operator using Luna High. Verified by human review.

For the reproduction using ngcc-harness https://github.com/AskusLi/ngcc-harness/tree/Aigis-reproduction/sign-01 

The wrapper and the extra unpack were read from the published reference tree:

- `Aigis-Sig+-I/SIG_AlgorithmInstance.c`
- `Aigis-Sig+-I/polyvec.c`
- `Aigis-Sig+-I/polyvec.h`
- `Aigis-Sig+-I/params.h`

`PARAM_L` is 2, 4 and 7 for parameter sets I, II and III.

Complete drivers are included at the end of this message. They expect the harness link shims `link_common.h` / `link_sig.h` and a built `sig_sign` / `sig_verify` shared library.

---

## 1. sig_sign and sig_verify ignore key lengths and unpack short key buffers

The ICCS entry points take key lengths, but the reference wrapper does not use them. The underlying routines unpack fixed-size keys.

```c
int sig_sign(
    unsigned char *sk, unsigned long long sk_len_bytes,
    unsigned char *m, unsigned long long m_len_bytes,
    unsigned char *sn, unsigned long long *sn_len_bytes)
{
    return msig_sign(sk, m, m_len_bytes, sn, sn_len_bytes);
}

int sig_verify(
    unsigned char *pk, unsigned long long pk_len_bytes,
    unsigned char *sn, unsigned long long sn_len_bytes,
    unsigned char *m, unsigned long long m_len_bytes)
{
    return msig_verf(pk, sn, sn_len_bytes, m, m_len_bytes);
}
```

`sk_len_bytes` and `pk_len_bytes` are unused. `sig_get_sk_len_bytes()` and `sig_get_pk_len_bytes()` advertise the fixed sizes (2800 and 928 bytes on Aigis-sig1).

`msig_sign` / `msig_verf` pass the pointer to `unpack_sk` / `unpack_pk` with no length check. Those functions immediately read `SEEDBYTES` bytes from the key (`rho[i] = sk[i]` / `pk[i]`), then continue through the rest of the packed key.

The short-key driver first completes a full-size keygen / sign / verify. It then calls `sig_sign` and `sig_verify` in separate child processes with a one-byte key placed immediately before a `PROT_NONE` page and with declared length 0. Both children fault (`SIGSEGV` or `SIGBUS`). The only object adjacent to the guard page is the truncated key, so the fault is an access past that object. The test shows at least a two-byte read; the unpack source is what shows a full-key read.

Observed result:

```text
short-key-read full=accepted short_sign=guard-fault short_verify=guard-fault
CONFIRMED: truncated key buffers are unpacked
```

This is an out-of-bounds read of the key object. It can crash a process if the next page is inaccessible. It is a denial-of-service risk only if an application forwards an attacker-controlled short key into these functions. The test does not show memory disclosure, code execution, or a network-reachable path. A caller that uses the advertised `sig_get_*_len_bytes()` sizes never hits this behavior.

---

## 2. Honest signing writes one polynomial past polyvecl in polyvecl_uniform_gamma1

`polyvecl` is a vector of `PARAM_L` polynomials. `polyvecl_uniform_gamma1` unpacks `PARAM_L` elements and then calls `polyz_unpack` once more. After the loop, `i == PARAM_L`, so the extra call writes `v->vec[PARAM_L]`.

```c
typedef struct {
  poly vec[PARAM_L];
} polyvecl;

int polyvecl_uniform_gamma1(polyvecl *v, unsigned char* seed, unsigned int nonce)
{
    int i;
    unsigned char inbuf[SEEDBYTES + CRHBYTES + 2];
    unsigned char outbuf[SZBITS * PARAM_N / 8 + 1];
    for (i = 0; i < SEEDBYTES + CRHBYTES; ++i)
        inbuf[i] = seed[i];
    for (i = 0; i < PARAM_L ; i++)
    {
        inbuf[SEEDBYTES + CRHBYTES] = nonce & 0xFF;
        inbuf[SEEDBYTES + CRHBYTES + 1] = nonce >> 8;
        KDF(outbuf, SZBITS * PARAM_N / 8, inbuf, SEEDBYTES + CRHBYTES + 2);
        polyz_unpack(v->vec + i, outbuf);
        nonce++;
    }
    polyz_unpack(v->vec + i, outbuf); /* i == PARAM_L */
    return 0;
}
```

`polyz_unpack` writes a full polynomial (`PARAM_N = 512` coefficients, 2048 bytes). Neighboring helpers (`polyvecl_uniform_eta1`, `polyvecl_ntt`, and the other `polyvecl_*` loops) stop at `PARAM_L` and have no extra iteration. The extra unpack reuses the last loop `outbuf`, so the written polynomial equals the last valid component of `y`.

`msig_sign` keeps `y` on the stack next to `yhat`, `z`, and `cs1`:

```c
polyvecl mat[PARAM_K], y, yhat, z, cs1;
...
polyvecl_uniform_gamma1(&y, key, nonce);
yhat = y;
```

The overflow driver first completes a full-size sign-and-verify on a control library, then repeats the same valid `sig_sign` against an AddressSanitizer build. It accepts only a diagnostic that contains both `stack-buffer-overflow` and `polyvecl_uniform_gamma1`.

Observed results, parameter set I:

```text
ordinary -O2 keygen/sign/verify: passed
-O2 + ASan valid sig_sign:      stack-buffer-overflow in polyvecl_uniform_gamma1
signing-stack-overflow full-round-trip=passed asan-sign=asan-diagnostic
```

The extra store is undefined behavior in C. It is still present at `-O2`: the `-O2` ASan build reports the write. The ordinary `-O2` binary completed a normal keygen / sign / verify round trip, so that run did not turn the write into a visible failure. The next stack object is layout-dependent. If it is `yhat`, the following `yhat = y` overwrites the smashed region. The test does not show a canary abort, controlled corruption, code execution, or key disclosure. An attacker must be able to cause an application to sign. The test does not show that an untrusted remote user can reach that service.

The extra call should be removed. After the loop, `i` is already `PARAM_L` and `v->vec[0 .. PARAM_L-1]` have been filled.

---

The first issue is repaired by checking `sk_len_bytes` and `pk_len_bytes` against `SIG_SECRETKEYBYTES` and `SIG_PUBLICKEYBYTES` before unpacking, and rejecting a short buffer. The second issue is repaired by deleting the extra `polyz_unpack`.

Optimized (AVX2 / NEON) copies in the same archive were not checked here. The extra `polyz_unpack` line is in the published reference `polyvec.c` for parameter sets I, II and III. The guard-page driver and both `-O2` signing tests were run on parameter set I.

Best regards

Yijian_Liu

27 Sep 27 Sep
1:57 p.m.

Hi, I believe the challenge sampler in the Aigis-Sig+ 256-bit parameter set contains a sign-handling error that reduces its min-entropy below the claimed security level. In particular, Algorithm 24 (`SampleInBall`) in the specification assigns an independent sign bit to each of the tau nonzero coefficients. However, in the `PARAM_C <= 64` branch of the submitted implementation, the loop in `unpack_c()` contains: ``` c->coeffs[b] = 1 - 2 * (signs & 1); signs = 0; ``` The second line appears to be an error: it clears all remaining sign bits after the first iteration. Consequently, for Aigis-Sig+-II (n=512, tau=44), only one sign bit remains effective, while the other 43 signs are fixed to +1. The resulting min-entropy is: H_\infty = \log_2 \binom{512}{44} + 1 \approx 213.46 \text{ bits}, which is below the claimed 256-bit security level. Parameter set Claimed level Implemented min-entropy Shortfall ---------------- ------------- ----------------------- ------------ Aigis-Sig-II 256 bits 213.46 bits 42.53 bits The same loop update is present in the reference, AVX2, NEON, and AArch64 implementations. The initialization `signs = 0` before loading the sign bytes is correct; only the `signs = 0` statement inside the sampling loop should be replaced with: ``` signs >>= 1; ``` Parameter set III uses the separate `PARAM_C > 64` branch and is not affected by this issue. This analysis was prepared with AI assistance. (Identified by Doubao) Best, Yijian

RunqingXu

3:13 p.m.
Dear all,

We sincerely thank you for reporting the implementation errors in our submitted Aigis-Sig+ code. Some of them—including the sign-handling issue reported today by Yijian—have already been fixed in the updated Reference and AVX2 implementations attached in our first comment posted on September 22 at 11:32 a.m.

We have continued to fix implementation errors and improve code quality, and we have updated the Aigis-Sig+ implementation to version 1.0.1. The latest implementation is provided in the attachment. Below is a summary of the updates:

1. Changed the signature encoding to fixed length, with zero padding for unused hint bits and bytes.
2. Added checks for invalid hint section markers, excessive hint counts, duplicate or out-of-order positions, and nonzero padding during signature verification.
3. Fixed incorrect handling of random sign bits in challenge polynomial c generation for parameter sets I and II in the REF, AVX2, and ARM implementations.
4. Added checks for key, signature, and message lengths and the signature-length output pointer, and reset the output length to zero on signing failure.
5. Fixed temporary-buffer memory leaks on verification failure paths.
6. Fixed the handling of remaining random data and refill logic in AVX2 seed-based sampling of secret vectors s1 and s2.
7. Removed an extra unpacking call after sampling the polynomial vector y during REF signing, fixing an out-of-bounds write past the end of the vector.
8. Fixed out-of-bounds reads and writes in AVX2 encoding, decoding, and rejection sampling for matrix generation, as well as SIMD tail-block overreads in NEON hint encoding and decoding.
9. Fixed undefined behavior when left-shifting negative coefficients during REF verification, along with unaligned accesses and type-aliasing violations in sparse polynomial multiplication.
10. Added explicit alignment for AVX2 NTT constant tables and corrected pointer types and const qualifiers in REF and AVX2.
11. Corrected the pointer types used for timing data in REF and AVX2 benchmark functions.
12. Aligned ARM parameter definitions and KDF calls with the reference implementation, including input concatenation order, input lengths, and the KDF selected for each parameter set.
13. Removed unused implementations and redundant header files from REF and AVX2.

We appreciate the community's continued feedback and analysis, which help us improve the correctness and robustness of our implementations.

We welcome further analysis and comments from the community.

Best regards,  
The Aigis-Sig+ Team

1 Oct 1 Oct
4:35 p.m.

Dear Aigis-Sig+ team, We found a numerical inconsistency in the security analysis of the Aigis-Sig+ specification: the abort-probability bound p̄ of §7.3, evaluated at the specification's own parameters, exceeds 1 for two of the three parameter sets. A probability bound greater than 1 bounds nothing. The facts. Section 7.3 computes p̄ — the upper bound on the signing abort probability — as the sum of two event probabilities (exponents a = nℓβ1/γ1 and b = nk(β2+η1)/γ2 over the Table 1 parameters). Evaluating this at the delivered parameter sets gives: PARAMSI: p̄ = 1.0767 PARAMSII: p̄ = 0.980 PARAMSIII: p̄ = 1.1609 The cross-check holds: the Table 2 repetition rates (6.41/5.16/5.71) match e^{a+b} = 6.40/5.16/5.71, so the inputs are the specification's own. Meanwhile Theorems 1 and 2 use p̄ under the explicit precondition 0 < p̄ < 1, stated in four places (§7.1, §7.2, A.4, B.3), and §7.3 characterizes the result as a "reasonably sized constant". As printed, the formula violates its own precondition for PARAMSI and PARAMSIII — the two events can occur simultaneously, and their sum double-counts the overlap. For what this does and does not affect: the theorems themselves are not falsified — a valid bound exists (the measured abort rates are 0.844/0.806/0.825), and the ε-term conclusions of Appendix A do not depend on p̄. What fails is the printed analysis: a precondition of the proof's quantitative chain is violated by the specification's own arithmetic; and for PARAMSII, substituting the printed p̄ into the proof's B2 coefficients yields values (around 2^93 and 2^176) that the specification never evaluates. We bring this to the team's attention. This analysis was prepared with AI assistance (GLM-5.3). Best regards, Sun Shuzhou

RunqingXu

6:27 p.m.
Dear Sun Shuzhou,

Thank you for pointing out this inconsistency. It stems from our use of an overly loose upper bound, \(\bar{p}\) — the signing abort probability bound — as the sum of two event probabilities, with exponents \(a = n\ell\beta_1/\gamma_1\) and \(b = nk(\beta_2+\eta_1)/\gamma_2\). A tighter estimate is

\[
\bar{p} \approx 1 - \exp(-a-b),
\]

which is also consistent with your measured abort rates.

Since the security proof only requires the existence of a bound \(\bar{p} < 1\), the security claim is unaffected, as you noted. Thank you again.

We welcome further analysis, comments, and feedback from the community.

Best regards,  
The Aigis-Sig+ Team
